name: Aleppo earthquake of 1138
summary: Long-duration earthquake sequence in Syria's Dead Sea Transform zone in autumn 1138 levels much of Aleppo and the surrounding Atharib citadel. Medieval chroniclers (Ibn al-Athir, Bar Hebraeus) report 230,000 dead, likely exaggerated but still among the deadliest medieval seismic events.

_quarry.structural_significance: Catastrophic damage in northern Syria coincides with the consolidation of Zengi's emirate; cities in ruins are rebuilt under his successor Nur al-Din with stronger fortifications that later resist Crusader sieges through the 1180s.
